title: Purpose and Result Clauses
objectives: Recognize purpose clauses with ut/ne + subjunctive
Recognize result clauses with ut/ut non + subjunctive
Distinguish purpose from result by context and signpost words
Translate purpose and result clauses idiomatically

vocabulary.definition: so that, in order that (purpose); so that, with the result that (result)
so, in such a way (signals result)

grammar.explanation: Purpose clauses tell why an action is done (goal). Result clauses tell what happens as a consequence (outcome). Both use ut + subjunctive, but they differ in negation and signpost words.

paradigms.name: Purpose vs Result
rows: ut non, ut nemo, ut nihil

rules: Purpose negative = ne; Result negative = ut non
Result clauses have signpost words in main clause
Both use subjunctive (sequence of tenses applies)
Relative clause of purpose: qui/quae/quod + subjunctive

exercises.question: Purpose or result? 'Tam fortiter pugnavit ut hostes fugerent.'
exercises.answer: Result - tam is a signpost word

exercises.question: Translate: Veni ut viderem.
exercises.answer: I came in order to see. / I came so that I might see.

readingPassage.latin: Caesar milites misit ut pontem facerent. Milites tam celeriter laboraverunt ut pons intra tres dies perfectus esset. Legatos misit qui pacem peterent.
readingPassage.translation: Caesar sent soldiers to build a bridge (purpose). The soldiers worked so quickly that the bridge was completed within three days (result). He sent envoys to seek peace (relative purpose).
notes: Note the different clause types and their translations
